records.source: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְאָ֫סָ֥ףאַ֤ךְ ט֭וֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֱלֹהִ֗ים לְבָרֵ֥י לֵבָֽב׃
records.gloss: A psalm of Asaph. Surely good to Israel [is] God, to [the] pure of heart.
pieces: A psalm of Asaph. \q God really is good to Israel, \q to people with a clean heart.

L.1: A psalm of Asaph. \q Surely God [is] good to Israel, \q to [the] pure of heart.

R.1: A song of Asaph. \q It is true: God is good to Israel, \q to everyone whose heart is pure.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the first psalm of Book Three
decisions.reason: Psalm 73 opens the third of the five books of the Psalms (Psalms 73-89), and the group of eleven psalms of Asaph (73-83).

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work. Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: surely: truly, after all
decisions.reason: The word ('akh) affirms something against doubt. It opens the psalm's conclusion before its struggle, and comes back at its turning points (verses 13, 18).

decisions.choice: pure of heart: true and clean within
decisions.reason: As in 24:4: people whose inner life and motives are clean before God.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

records.heading: Envy of the wicked, and nearness to God

records.source: וַאֲנִ֗י כִּ֭מְעַט נָטָ֣יוּ רַגְלָ֑י כְּ֝אַ֗יִן שֻׁפְּכ֥וּ אֲשֻׁרָֽי׃
records.gloss: But I — like a little, my feet had turned aside; like nothing, my steps had been poured out.
pieces: But I came close to losing my footing; \q my steps very nearly slid out from under me.

L.2: But as for me, my feet had almost turned aside; \q my steps had nearly slipped.

R.2: But I almost lost my way. \q I very nearly fell away from God.

decisions.choice: the words as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Both verbs are marked to be read in a different form from the one written; the sense is the same, "turned aside" and "slipped".

decisions.choice: my feet had almost slipped: I nearly lost my faith
decisions.reason: The picture is of losing one's footing on a path (17:5; 38:17). Here it is his trust in God's goodness (verse 1) that nearly gave way.

decisions.choice: I almost lost my way; I nearly fell away from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: כִּֽי־קִ֭נֵּאתִי בַּֽהוֹלְלִ֑ים שְׁל֖וֹם רְשָׁעִ֣ים אֶרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: For I was jealous of the boastful; [the] peace of [the] wicked I saw.
pieces: I had grown jealous of the proud, \q watching wicked people do well.

L.3: For I was jealous of the boastful; \q I saw [the] peace of [the] wicked.

R.3: I was jealous of proud people. \q I saw that evil people have an easy life.

decisions.choice: the boastful: the arrogant
decisions.reason: The word (holelim) is those who boast, as in 5:6 and 75:5.

decisions.choice: peace: well-being, success
decisions.reason: The word (shalom) here is the ease and success of the wicked, all going well for them.

decisions.choice: Psalm 37:1
decisions.reason: Psalm 37:1 warns against this envy: "Do not be jealous of those who do wrong".

records.source: כִּ֤י אֵ֖ין חַרְצֻבּ֥וֹת לְמוֹתָ֗ם וּבָרִ֥יא אוּלָֽם׃
records.gloss: For there are no pains at their death, and fat [is] their body.
pieces: They die without pain, \q and their bodies are plump and healthy.

L.4: For there are no pains at their death, \q and their body [is] fat.

R.4: They do not suffer, even when they die. \q Their bodies are healthy and well fed.

decisions.choice: no pains at their death
alternatives: they have no pains; their body is sound and fat (dividing the words differently)
decisions.reason: The letters can also be divided to read "they have no pains; sound and fat is their body", which keeps the verse on their life rather than their death. The text as divided speaks of an easy death.

decisions.choice: fat: well fed
decisions.reason: Being fat was a sign of plenty and health (92:15), not a fault.

records.source: בַּעֲמַ֣ל אֱנ֣וֹשׁ אֵינֵ֑מוֹ וְעִם־אָ֝דָ֗ם לֹ֣א יְנֻגָּֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: In [the] trouble of man they are not, and with mankind they are not struck.
pieces: They are free from the hardships others carry; \q they are not plagued like the rest of humankind.

L.5: They are not in the trouble of [other] people, \q and with [other] people they are not struck.

R.5: They do not have the troubles other people have. \q They do not suffer like everyone else.

decisions.choice: man, mankind: ordinary people
decisions.reason: The two words ('enosh, 'adam) both mean human beings: the wicked seem to escape the common lot of mortals.

decisions.choice: struck: struck by trouble or sickness
decisions.reason: The verb (naga') is used of being struck by disease or by God's hand; verse 14 uses it of the speaker himself.

records.source: לָ֭כֵן עֲנָקַ֣תְמוֹ גַאֲוָ֑ה יַעֲטָף־שִׁ֝֗ית חָמָ֥ס לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore pride [is] their necklace; a garment of violence covers them.
pieces: So they wear pride like a chain around the neck, \q and violence wraps them like a robe.

L.6: Therefore pride [is] their necklace; \q a garment of violence covers them.

R.6: So they show off their pride like a necklace. \q They wear violence like clothes.

decisions.choice: pride a necklace, violence a garment: worn openly
decisions.reason: They display their pride and their violence as proudly as jewelry and fine clothes, for all to see.

records.source: יָ֭צָא מֵחֵ֣לֶב עֵינֵ֑מוֹ עָ֝בְר֗וּ מַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת לֵבָֽב׃
records.gloss: It goes out from fat, their eye; they pass over, [the] imaginations of [the] heart.
pieces: Their eyes bulge from their fat faces; \q the fancies of their minds run past all limits.

L.7: Their eye bulges out from fat; \q the imaginations of [their] heart overflow.

R.7: They are so fat that their eyes bulge. \q Their heads are full of foolish plans.

decisions.choice: their eye
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation read a word with almost the same letters, "their wrongdoing comes out from fat", that is, from hearts dulled by plenty (17:10).

decisions.choice: imaginations: what their minds dream up
decisions.reason: The word (maskiyyot) is something imagined or pictured; their pride and plans know no limit.

records.source: יָמִ֤יקוּ׀וִידַבְּר֣וּ בְרָ֣ע עֹ֑שֶׁק מִמָּר֥וֹם יְדַבֵּֽרוּ׃
records.gloss: They mock and they speak with evil [of] oppression; from on high they speak.
pieces: They jeer and talk of evil; \q from on high they speak of crushing others.

L.8: They mock and speak with evil [of] oppression; \q from on high they speak.

R.8: They make fun of others and say cruel things. \q They act as if they were above everyone, and they threaten to hurt people.

decisions.choice: speak with evil of oppression
alternatives: speak with evil; they speak of oppression from on high
decisions.reason: The word "oppression" can go with the first half or the second; the meaning is much the same: they talk of crushing others.

decisions.choice: from on high: from a lofty height, looking down on others
decisions.reason: They speak as if they sat above everyone, even with God's authority (verse 9).

records.source: שַׁתּ֣וּ בַשָּׁמַ֣יִם פִּיהֶ֑ם וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם תִּֽהֲלַ֥ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: They set in the heavens their mouth, and their tongue walks in the earth.
pieces: Their mouths speak as if they owned heaven; \q their tongues go swaggering through the land.

L.9: They set their mouth in the heavens, \q and their tongue walks through the earth.

R.9: They talk as if they ruled heaven. \q They say whatever they like about everything on earth.

decisions.choice: set their mouth in the heavens: speak as if they ruled heaven and earth
alternatives: set their mouth against the heavens
decisions.reason: Their talk reaches up to heaven and over all the earth: they speak against God and lord it over people.

records.source: לָכֵ֤ן׀יָשׁ֣וּב עַמּ֣וֹ הֲלֹ֑ם וּמֵ֥י מָ֝לֵ֗א יִמָּ֥צוּ לָֽמוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore his people turn back here, and waters of fullness are drained by them.
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people turn their way \q and gulp down their words like water from a full cup.

L.10: Therefore {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people turn back here, \q and waters of fullness are drained by them.

R.10: So even God's people turn to follow them. \q They take in everything those people say, as if they were drinking water.

decisions.choice: turn back: the word as read, not as written
alternatives: he brings his people back here (as written)
decisions.reason: The word is written as "he brings back" and marked to be read as "they turn back". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: his people turn here and drink: people are drawn to the wicked
alternatives: God's people turn back to this question
decisions.reason: The verse is one of the hardest in the psalm. "His people" is most likely God's people, who turn to the wicked and take in their talk as freely as water. Others read it of the wicked man's followers.

decisions.choice: God's people
decisions.reason: Readable names whose people are meant, following the likeliest reading (m2).

records.source: וְֽאָמְר֗וּ אֵיכָ֥ה יָדַֽע־אֵ֑ל וְיֵ֖שׁ דֵּעָ֣ה בְעֶלְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And they say, How does God know? And is there knowledge with [the] Most High?
pieces: And they ask, "What can God know? \q Is the Most High aware of anything?"

L.11: And they say, "How does God know? \q And is there knowledge with [the] Most High?"

R.11: They say, "God cannot know what we do. \q The God who is above all does not see it."

decisions.choice: how does God know: God does not notice
decisions.reason: The question is a scoffing denial, as in 10:11 and 94:7: the wicked act as if God does not see or care.

decisions.choice: the Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5.

decisions.choice: statements
alternatives: How does God know? Is there knowledge with the Most High?
decisions.reason: Readable turns the scoffing questions into the claims they make (m1), and says "the God who is above all" for "the Most High".

records.source: הִנֵּה־אֵ֥לֶּה רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְשַׁלְוֵ֥י ע֝וֹלָ֗ם הִשְׂגּוּ־חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: Look, these [are the] wicked, and always at ease they have increased wealth.
pieces: So these are the wicked: \q never troubled, always growing richer.

L.12: Look, these [are the] wicked, \q and always at ease they have increased [in] wealth.

R.12: Look at these evil people! \q They never have a care, and they keep getting richer.

decisions.choice: always at ease: untroubled for ever
decisions.reason: The word (shalev) is the quiet ease of those with nothing to fear.

records.source: אַךְ־רִ֭יק זִכִּ֣יתִי לְבָבִ֑י וָאֶרְחַ֖ץ בְּנִקָּי֣וֹן כַּפָּֽי׃
records.gloss: Surely in vain I have kept pure my heart and washed in innocence my hands.
pieces: So it was for nothing that I kept my heart clean \q and washed my hands to show I was innocent.

L.13: Surely in vain I have kept my heart pure \q and washed my hands in innocence.

R.13: It seemed useless for me to keep my heart pure \q and to stay away from doing wrong.

decisions.choice: surely in vain: what he thought then
decisions.reason: Verses 13-14 give the bitter thought he had before he went into God's sanctuary (verse 17). "Surely" ('akh) answers the "surely" of verse 1.

decisions.choice: washed my hands in innocence: kept myself free of guilt
decisions.reason: Washing the hands was a sign of innocence (26:6; Deuteronomy 21:6-7).

decisions.choice: stay away from doing wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

records.source: וָאֱהִ֣י נָ֭גוּעַ כָּל־הַיּ֑וֹם וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לַבְּקָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I have been struck all the day, and my rebuke [was] every morning.
pieces: I have been beaten down the whole day long, \q and corrected afresh each morning.

L.14: For I have been struck all the day, \q and my punishment [came] every morning.

R.14: I suffer all day long. \q Every morning I am punished again.

decisions.choice: rebuke: correction, punishment
decisions.reason: The word (tokechah) is a rebuke or correction; his suffering felt like God's punishment though he had kept himself pure.

decisions.choice: every morning: day after day
decisions.reason: "To the mornings" means each morning, again and again.

records.source: אִם־אָ֭מַרְתִּי אֲסַפְּרָ֥ה כְמ֑וֹ הִנֵּ֤ה ד֭וֹר בָּנֶ֣יךָ בָגָֽדְתִּי׃
records.gloss: If I had said, I will speak thus, look, [the] generation of your children I would have betrayed.
pieces: Had I resolved to speak like this, \q I would have broken faith with the family of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} children.

L.15: If I had said I would speak like this, \q look, I would have betrayed the generation of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} children.

R.15: If I had told others what I was thinking, \q I would have let down all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

decisions.choice: the generation of your children: God's people
decisions.reason: The "children" are God's children, the community of those who belong to him (Deuteronomy 14:1); "generation" is the circle of the faithful (14:5; 24:6).

decisions.choice: betrayed: been false to
decisions.reason: The verb (bagad) is to break faith. To voice his doubts as truth would have been to abandon his fellow believers.

decisions.choice: told others what I was thinking
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that "like this" refers to the thoughts of verses 13-14.

records.source: וָֽ֭אֲחַשְּׁבָה לָדַ֣עַת זֹ֑את עָמָ֖ל ה֣וּא בְעֵינָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I thought to understand this; trouble it [was] in my eyes,
pieces: So I tried to make sense of it, \q but it seemed a weary task to me,

L.16: And I thought [how] to understand this; \q it [was] trouble in my eyes,

R.16: I tried to understand all this. \q But it was too hard for me.

decisions.choice: it: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The written and read forms differ only in spelling; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: "Until" in verse 17 finishes the thought, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.source: עַד־אָ֭בוֹא אֶל־מִקְדְּשֵׁי־אֵ֑ל אָ֝בִ֗ינָה לְאַחֲרִיתָֽם׃
records.gloss: until I came into [the] sanctuaries of God; I understood their end.
pieces: until I entered God's holy place; \q then I saw where they will end.

L.17: until I went into the sanctuary of God; \q [then] I understood their end.

R.17: Then I went into God's temple. \q There I understood what will happen to them in the end.

decisions.choice: the sanctuaries of God: God's holy place
decisions.reason: The plural may mean the temple and its courts, or be a plural of majesty for the one sanctuary (68:36). There, in God's presence, the speaker sees things as they are.

decisions.choice: their end: what finally becomes of them
decisions.reason: The word ('acharit) is the end or outcome, the last part of the story (37:37-38).

decisions.choice: the turning point of the psalm
decisions.reason: Worship changes his view: verses 18-28 answer verses 2-16.

records.source: אַ֣ךְ בַּ֭חֲלָקוֹת תָּשִׁ֣ית לָ֑מוֹ הִ֝פַּלְתָּ֗ם לְמַשּׁוּאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Surely on slippery [places] you set them; you make them fall to ruins.
pieces: In fact, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have set them where the footing is slick, \q and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} let them crash into ruin.

L.18: Surely on slippery [places] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} set them; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} make them fall to ruin.

R.18: You have put them in a place where they can easily slip. \q You make them fall and be destroyed.

decisions.choice: slippery places: the answer to verse 2
decisions.reason: He thought his own feet were slipping (verse 2); now he sees that it is the wicked who stand on slippery ground (35:6).

decisions.choice: ruins: destruction
decisions.reason: The word (mashshu'ot) is found only here and in 74:3. It probably means ruins; a similar word means deceptions.

records.source: אֵ֤יךְ הָי֣וּ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה כְרָ֑גַע סָ֥פוּ תַ֝֗מּוּ מִן־בַּלָּהֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: How they have become a desolation in a moment! They have come to an end; they are finished from terrors.
pieces: In an instant they are ruined! \q Sudden terrors make an end of them.

L.19: How they have become a desolation in a moment! \q They have come to an end, they are finished by terrors.

R.19: In a moment they are destroyed! \q Terrible things happen to them, and they are gone.

decisions.choice: terrors: sudden dread and death
decisions.reason: The word (ballahot) is used of the terrors of death and disaster (Job 18:11, 14).

records.source: כַּחֲל֥וֹם מֵהָקִ֑יץ אֲ֝דֹנָי בָּעִ֤יר׀צַלְמָ֬ם תִּבְזֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Like a dream after waking, Lord, when [you] rouse [yourself], their image you will despise.
pieces: They are like a dream once the sleeper wakes; \q Lord, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stir, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will scorn them as mere shadows.

L.20: Like a dream after waking, \q my Lord, when [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}] rouse [{{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}], {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will despise their image.

R.20: They are like a dream that is gone when a person wakes up. \q Lord, when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} get up to act, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will treat them as if they were nothing.

decisions.choice: their image: their shadowy form
decisions.reason: The word (tselem) is an image or likeness; here, a shadow without substance (39:7). Like a dream, the success of the wicked vanishes when God acts.

decisions.choice: when you rouse yourself: when God acts
decisions.reason: God seems to sleep while evil goes on and "wakes" when he steps in (44:24). The same letters can be read "in the city".

decisions.choice: my Lord (L); Lord (B, R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, 'Adonai in address is "my Lord" at Literal and "Lord" at Balanced and Readable.

records.source: כִּ֭י יִתְחַמֵּ֣ץ לְבָבִ֑י וְ֝כִלְיוֹתַ֗י אֶשְׁתּוֹנָֽן׃
records.gloss: When my heart was embittered and [in] my kidneys I was pierced,
pieces: When my heart had turned sour \q and I felt stabbed deep inside,

L.21: When my heart was embittered, \q and I was pierced in my kidneys,

R.21: My heart was bitter, \q and I was hurt deep inside.

decisions.choice: kidneys: the inner self, the feelings
decisions.reason: The kidneys were thought of as the seat of the deepest feelings (7:10; 16:7).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The "when" clause is completed in verse 22, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: deep inside
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture (m1); Balanced does too.

records.source: וַאֲנִי־בַ֭עַר וְלֹ֣א אֵדָ֑ע בְּ֝הֵמ֗וֹת הָיִ֥יתִי עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: and I [was] stupid and did not know; [like] beasts I was with you.
pieces: I was a fool and knew nothing; \q in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence I was no better than an animal.

L.22: then I [was] stupid and did not know; \q [like] a beast I was before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

R.22: I was foolish and did not understand. \q I acted like an animal that cannot think, right in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: beasts: a dumb animal
decisions.reason: The plural (behemot) can mean one large beast (Job 40:15). He confesses that in his bitterness he was as senseless as an animal.

decisions.choice: like
decisions.reason: "A beast I was" is a comparison; the levels say "like" or "no better than".

records.source: וַאֲנִ֣י תָמִ֣יד עִמָּ֑ךְ אָ֝חַ֗זְתָּ בְּיַד־יְמִינִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I [am] continually with you; you hold [me by] my right hand.
pieces: Even so, I am with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at all times; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have taken me by the right hand.

L.23: Yet I [am] continually with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have held my right hand.

R.23: But I am always close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You hold me by the hand.

decisions.choice: continually with you: God stayed with him
decisions.reason: Even when he was senseless (verse 22), God did not let him go. The faith of verse 1 returns, now tested.

decisions.choice: you hold my right hand: you lead and keep me
decisions.reason: As a parent or a king takes someone by the hand (Isaiah 41:13; 42:6).

records.source: בַּעֲצָתְךָ֥ תַנְחֵ֑נִי וְ֝אַחַ֗ר כָּב֥וֹד תִּקָּחֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: With your counsel you will guide me, and after, [to] glory you will take me.
pieces: You lead me by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wise advice, \q and at the end {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me up in glory.

L.24: With {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} counsel {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} guide me, \q and afterward {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me [to] glory.

R.24: You guide me by showing me what is wise. \q And at the end {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will take me to be with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in glory.

decisions.choice: afterward you will take me to glory: beyond this life
alternatives: afterward you will receive me with honor
you will lead me after glory
decisions.reason: "Take" (laqach) is the word used when God took Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3, 5), and in 49:16, "God will ransom my life from Sheol, for he will take me". Set against the sudden end of the wicked (verses 18-19), it points to life with God after death, though it may mean honor in this life.

decisions.choice: to be with you
decisions.reason: Readable says where God will take him, following the likeliest sense (m1).

records.source: מִי־לִ֥י בַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְ֝עִמְּךָ֗ לֹא־חָפַ֥צְתִּי בָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Who [is] for me in the heavens? And with you I do not delight in [anything] on the earth.
pieces: Who else is there for me in heaven? \q And having {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, I want nothing on earth.

L.25: Who [is there] for me in the heavens? \q And with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I desire nothing on the earth.

R.25: In heaven I have no one but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q And since I have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, there is nothing on earth I want.

decisions.choice: who is for me in heaven: no one but you
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one but you"; with God, nothing on earth is worth wanting.

decisions.choice: with you: having you, besides you
decisions.reason: The word ('im) is "with": being with God, he wants nothing else.

decisions.choice: I have no one but you
alternatives: Who is there for me in heaven?
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m1).

records.source: כָּלָ֥ה שְׁאֵרִ֗י וּלְבָ֫בִ֥י צוּר־לְבָבִ֥י וְחֶלְקִ֗י אֱלֹהִ֥ים לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: It has failed, my flesh and my heart; [the] rock of my heart and my portion [is] God forever.
pieces: Though body and heart wear out, \q God is the rock my heart rests on and the share that is mine forever.

L.26: My flesh and my heart have failed; \q [the] rock of my heart and my portion [is] God forever.

R.26: My body and my mind may grow weak. \q But God is like a rock that holds up my heart. He is all I need forever.

decisions.choice: my portion: my share, all I have
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is a share of land. The priests had no land; God was their portion (Numbers 18:20; Psalm 16:5). So God is all the speaker owns.

decisions.choice: has failed: or may fail
decisions.reason: The verb is in the past tense: his body and heart are worn out, or even if they fail, God remains.

decisions.choice: the rock of my heart: the strength of my inner life
decisions.reason: God is the firm rock under him (18:3), holding up his heart when it fails.

records.source: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה רְחֵקֶ֣יךָ יֹאבֵ֑דוּ הִ֝צְמַ֗תָּה כָּל־זוֹנֶ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ׃
records.gloss: For look, those far from you will perish; you destroy everyone who acts as a prostitute from you.
pieces: Those who move far from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are lost; \q everyone who deserts {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to love another, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cut off.

L.27: For look, those far from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will perish; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} destroy everyone who strays from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in unfaithfulness.

R.27: People who stay far away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will die. \q You destroy everyone who turns away from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to worship other gods.

decisions.choice: acts as a prostitute from you: is unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: The prophets picture Israel's turning to other gods as a wife's unfaithfulness to her husband (Hosea 1:2; Jeremiah 3:1).

decisions.choice: deserts you to love another (B); turns away from you to worship other gods (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of unfaithful love; Readable says what it means (m1).

decisions.choice: strays from you in unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the sense of the verb in words fit for public reading.

records.source: וַאֲנִ֤י׀קִֽרֲבַ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֗ים לִ֫י־ט֥וֹב שַׁתִּ֤י׀בַּאדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֣ה מַחְסִ֑י לְ֝סַפֵּ֗ר כָּל־מַלְאֲכוֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And I — [the] nearness of God for me [is] good; I have made in [the] Lord YHWH my refuge, to recount all your works.
pieces: As for me, being close to God is my good; \q in the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} I have found my shelter, \q and I will tell of all {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

L.28: But as for me, [the] nearness of God [is] good for me; \q I have made the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my refuge, \q to recount all {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works.

R.28: But for me, the best thing is to be close to God. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} is where I go to be safe. \q I will tell everyone about all the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done.

decisions.choice: the nearness of God is good: the psalm's answer
decisions.reason: The psalm began, "God is good to Israel" (verse 1); it ends with what that good is: to be near God. The "far from you" of verse 27 is its opposite.

decisions.choice: the Lord YHWH
decisions.reason: As in 71:5, the title followed by the divine name.

decisions.choice: your works: speaking to God again
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of God, then turns to him in the last words.
